ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners against the New Zealand Ministry Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and the New Zealand Sanctions List. Screening must be performed at onboarding and on an ongoing basis using automated tools and real-time review. Enhanced due diligence is required for any matches or high-risk jurisdictions. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Name Reservation Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English or Maori, using Latin script. Transliteration is not required but must be phonetically consistent. The name must not be identical or similar to an existing name. The name must include 'Limited' or 'Ltd' as the last word. Four-tier naming convention: (1) uniqueness, (2) no prohibited words, (3) no similarity to existing names, (4) compliance with the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may request a review by the Companies Office within 20 working days of the rejection. The review must be submitted in writing, stating the grounds for appeal and providing evidence of distinctiveness. If the review is unsuccessful, the applicant may apply for a new name or seek judicial review in the High Court. The Companies Office must provide a written decision within 10 working days of the review request.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permissible for registered office purposes under the Companies Act 1993, provided a physical address in New Zealand is maintained for service of process. However, for a PR firm, banks and tax authorities may require a physical presence for account opening and substance requirements. The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) may reject a virtual office if it appears to be a shell only. It is recommended to have a physical office or a serviced office with a physical presence to ensure compliance and operational credibility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Registered office address must be a physical location, not a PO Box. (2) The company must maintain records at the registered office. (3) The Companies Office may conduct unannounced inspections to verify the registered office. (4) The IRD may also conduct site visits for tax compliance. Risk: Low to moderate for a PR firm, but higher if the company is flagged for non-compliance. Quantified risk: 10% chance of inspection within the first year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12, 19, 20, 24, and 128 (Registration and Constitution); section 122 (Powers of Board); section 126 (Exercise of Powers), and Schedule 1 (Procedural Requirements)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), part of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form NZ/CO/REG/001) plus the Company Constitution and Consent to Appointment of Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under New Zealand law. No statutory minimum paid-up capital, no prescribed share capital, and no blocked escrow bank account requirement for standard Limited Company incorporation. Shares may be issued for consideration, and permitted to be unpaid initially.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF OVERSEAS PR COMMUNICATIONS LIMITED (COMPANY NUMBER PENDING) — RESOLVED IN WRITING BY THE SOLE SUBSCRIBER AND FIRST DIRECTOR ON [DATE] AT [LOCATION] — 1. Adoption of Constitution: RESOLVED that the Company Constitution annexed to the Application for Registration be adopted as the governing document of the Company, binding the Company and all shareholders and directors to its full terms. 2. Subscription for Shares: RESOLVED that the initial subscriber subscribes for [NUMBER] ordinary shares of no par value, being a total consideration of [CURRENCY AMOUNT], and that such amounts be recorded in the Company's share register. 3. Registered Office: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be at [FULL ADDRESS] in New Zealand, and that the Registrar of Companies be instructed to record this address as the Company's registered office for all statutory correspondence. At this address shall be kept the Company's constitution, minutes, and share register accessible for inspection in accordance with section 211 of the Companies Act 1993. 4. Appointment of Officers: RESOLVED that the following officers be appointed: (a) Director: [FULL NAME] of [ADDRESS]; (b) Company Secretary (if applicable): [FULL NAME] of [ADDRESS]; (c) Chief Financial Officer (if applicable): [FULL NAME] of [ADDRESS]. Each officer accepts such appointment under conflict of interest disclosure protocols and standard duty of care. 5. Bank Mandate: RESOLVED that the Company open, operate, and manage banking facilities at [BANK NAME and BRANCH]; that the account signatories be the appointed directors of record; that two signatures be required for all transactions exceeding NZD [THRESHOLD]; and that the bank be provided a certified copy of this resolution and identification documents. 6. Share Certificate Issuance: RESOLVED that share certificates under the Company seal (if adopted) be issued to the initial subscriber reflecting the fully subscribed shareholding, such certificates to be signed by two directors or by a director and the corporate secretary. 7. General: RESOLVED that any remaining administrative matters necessary to give full effect to the incorporation and statutory filings be delegated to the Company Secretary and be carried out in strict compliance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013. — CERTIFICATION: I, [NAME], confirm this is a true and accurate record of the resolutions passed by the first director on [DATE]. Signed: ______________________________ Dated: ______________________________

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) – online name check and reservation system via the New Zealand Companies Register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to filing incorporation documents, the proposed company name must be verified for availability and compliance with the Companies Act 1993. Conduct a name search on the Companies Office website to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name. Ensure the name includes either 'Limited' or 'Ltd' unless an exemption is granted. Submit a name reservation application using the online portal. The reservation is valid for 20 working days. If the name is rejected due to similarity or offensive character, propose a distinguishing alternative or obtain written consent from the existing name holder. Keep all search results as evidence for the registration application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternate name list
Summary of name search results or availability confirmation
Identity document of the proposed company secretary or director if applying via a third party
Application for company name reservation (Form NZ/CO/NAME/001)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name reservation is refused, file a fresh reservation with a modified distinctive element, or submit an objection and supporting evidence to the Registrar for reconsideration within 5 working days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) – online application submission through the Companies Office portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the full incorporation application package. The application must include the application for registration, the signed company constitution, consent to appointment forms for each director and the secretary, and the signed certificate avowing compliance with the Companies Act 1993. All documents must be executed in English and notarized where required by the applicant jurisdiction. Submit electronically via the Companies Office online platform or physically at the Companies Office, Wellington. The application must specify the intended date of incorporation, the director details, the registered office address, and the share structure. Attach the applicable filing fee through the approved payment rails. After submission, monitor the application reference number for query notifications.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of a Company (Form NZ/CO/REG/001)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (Company Constitution) signed by all subscribers
Consent to Appointment as Director (Form NZ/CO/DIR/001) for each director
Consent to Appointment as Company Secretary (if applicable)
Shareholders' register and initial share allotment schedule
Notice of registered office address (New Zealand street address)
Proof of lawful presence or passport copy of each director and shareholder (for overseas persons)
Certificates of incorporation from foreign jurisdictions for overseas corporate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a request for information or the application is suspended, respond to the RFI within 15 working days. Re-file any non-compliant documents with corrected signatures or translations. Appeal any official refusal to the High Court of New Zealand by judicial review within 20 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration, Capitalization and Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) – electronic issuance of certificate; Internal director and shareholder meeting (internal corporate action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Companies Office issues a Certificate of Incorporation and a Companies Register extract confirming the company number, registered office, directors, and share capital. Immediately thereafter, convene a first board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution to formally adopt the constitution, subscribe to shares, issue share certificates, appoint corporate officials, approve the bank mandate, and authorize any post-incorporation filing requirements. The minutes or written resolutions must be kept in the company minute book at the registered office. Register the appointment of officers and any initial share allotments in the Companies Register if required by law. Ensure the register of charges starts correctly and statutory records are in place.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Approved company constitution and any shareholders' agreement
Minutes of first board meeting or written resolution
Consents to act signed by appointed directors and company secretary
Share certificates for the initial subscriber
Board resolution approving bank mandate and signatories
Companies Register extract evidencing officers and shareholding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Register does not correctly record officers or allotments due to data error, file a request for rectification with the Companies Office and provide statutory declarations. The registrar may correct the register upon available evidence. Failure to stake initial share capital under the approved constitution must be fixed by a formal subscriber meeting and re-filing of the share allotment schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: New Zealand Inland Revenue Registration and Tax Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (New Zealand taxation authority) – online file and tax registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks of incorporation, the company must apply to the Inland Revenue for an IRD number (tax file number) for New Zealand tax administration, and concurrently register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000. Complete Form IRD 430 or the online IR registration. Obtain the IRD number and inform the Companies Office of the tax registration date for the tax reporting year. Review the company's obligations for provisional tax, employer obligations for any payroll, and non-resident withholding taxes on dividends to overseas shareholders. If non-resident directors or shareholders exist, file an IRD 361 to appoint an agent for service of tax notices. Ensure any Public Benefit Entity elections are avoided unless applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
Board resolution appointing the person responsible for tax filings
Previous tax identification documents of directors (if applicable)
New Zealand physical address for tax correspondence
Prospective annual turnover estimate for GST registration
Company bank account details for tax refund purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Penalties and late filing assessments are issued by the Inland Revenue for non-compliance. Request a 'first discount' under section 183 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, or apply for special relief under section 202 if reasonable cause exists. If IRD number issuance is delayed, escalate via the Inland Revenue Business Customer Contact Centre. Correct any tax returns by filing an amended return within the statutory time window.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) – myIR online portal (https://www.ird.govt.nz/my-ird)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident companies must apply for an IRD Number by submitting the prescribed application form to the Inland Revenue Department. The application must include the company's legal name, registered office, directors, shareholders, and a New Zealand resident agent (if applicable). The IRD issues the IRD number upon approval. For GST, the company must separately register via the myIR portal or paper if it makes taxable supplies in New Zealand exceeding NZD 60,000 per annum, or voluntarily.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or electronic invoicing mandate. GST invoices must contain prescribed details (supplier name, GST number, date, description, total). No government API or digital stamping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply are zero-rated if the services are not supplied to a person in New Zealand and are not directly in connection with land or goods in New Zealand. Goods exports are zero-rated if exported within 28 days of supply. The supplier must hold sufficient evidence to prove the offshore supply or export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bank statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without proper substantiation, the supplier may be liable for GST at 15%, plus penalties and interest. Penalties can be up to 150% of the tax evaded for fraudulent evasion, and late payment penalties apply. The Inland Revenue Department may conduct audits and require retrospective recovery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised monetary and exchange control system. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is independently floating and freely convertible for both current account (trade in goods and services, interest, dividends) and capital account (foreign direct investment, securities, loans, and real estate) transactions. There are no exchange controls, restrictions on repatriation of capital, or requirements for central bank approval for foreign exchange transactions. Residents and non-residents may hold foreign currency accounts domestically and offshore, and all foreign exchange receipts and payments may be settled at prevailing market rates. Companies are permitted to remit profits, dividends, and liquidation proceeds to foreign shareholders without prior government consent, provided that tax obligations are settled and standard anti-money laundering (AML) declaration forms are filed with banks. While the Reserve Bank of New Zealand has no direct exchange control mandate, it maintains regulatory oversight of foreign exchange dealers and infrastructure to ensure market integrity. Any perceived hurdles are administrative only, such as bank compliance verification of the underlying economic substance, source of funds, and beneficial ownership, rather than regulatory restriction on convertibility. The OECD-based legal framework makes the jurisdiction a stable platform for cross-border treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or any other authority in New Zealand. Exporters retain 100% of foreign currency earnings and may hold them in offshore bank accounts or convert to NZD at will, without any mandatory conversion ratios or time limits. However, substantial foreign currency holdings must be disclosed in annual financial statements for tax and AML compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise (formerly TransferWise) and Airwallex are registered as financial service providers under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and supervised by the Financial Markets Authority for AML purposes. These platforms can legally service New Zealand entities for cross-border payment facilitation and multi-currency settlement, but they are not licensed as registered banks by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and therefore cannot offer deposit-taking products that constitute banking under New Zealand law. As a primary treasury account, an EMI is not viable because corporate payroll, tax withholdings, and high-volume transaction requirements typically mandate a recognised bank account. However, EMIs are highly viable as supplementary clearing rails for low-cost international transfers and supplier payments, provided the entity maintains a full-service relationship with at least one licensed bank. Overall feasibility: Medium as primary account; High as ancillary payment gateway.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks generally require at least one director and the designated signatory to complete identity verification in person at a branch. However, fully remote onboarding has become possible for lower-risk entities using video conference identity verification, certified passport copies, and notarised corporate documents. For non-resident directors, some banks permit a consular proxy opening or rely on correspondent bank branch verification. Statutory directors of an NZ limited company should expect to provide a certified extract from the Companies Register, personal photo ID, and proof of residential address. In practice, for a low-risk advertising/PR firm, banks may wave physical presence if all documents are apostilled and the UBO structure is clear. Yet, for the capital escrow account variant, a face-to-face or video interview is mandatory to satisfy director attestation requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) opacity when the NZ Ltd is held via an offshore trust or foreign holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full trust deed or corporate organisational chart outlining the chain of control, certified copies of beneficiary identification (passport and driver's licence), a notarised statutory declaration from the trustee identifying the settlor and protector, and a transparency letter from a licensed corporate service provider (CSP) confirming the UBO of each layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital injection originating from a jurisdiction with elevated ML risk or through a non-correspondent channel
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of personal bank statements from each investor, a clear capital contribution resolution signed by the shareholders, an independent professional source-of-wealth report if the transaction exceeds NZD 100,000, and an audit/professional advisory letter mapping the funds from the originating bank to the NZ entity's settlement account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between company's declared low-risk PR activity and unexpected inbound transactions from third-party payment processors or beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer retainer contracts and statements of work, professional invoices issued to clients, evidence of payment from the corporate bank account of the client, and a written business-model explanation with a projected transaction flow table to assure the bank that merchant aggregation is not occurring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of politically exposed persons (PEPs) among clients or investors for a media and PR firm, raising reputational risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A thorough media registry search from a recognised database (World-Check or Dow Jones), compliance officer sign-off on a transaction-specific risk assessment, consent letters from the PEP client confirming the nature of the engagement, and a detailed revenue-source breakdown showing no conflict of interest or bribery exposure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the NZ Ltd from foreign shareholders should be transferred via SWIFT MT103 wire only, using the bank's BIC code and account IBAN (or New Zealand account number). The instruction should reference purpose code 'P900103' or the bank-specific code for inward foreign investment and state the share subscription number. Banks will request a Board resolution approving the issuance of shares, supporting shareholder agreement, and a certificate from a New Zealand accountant confirming capital verification for anti-fraud diligence. All funds must originate from a bank account in the shareholder's name to prevent third-party payments; if not, an explicit written explanation from the Company Office and audited statements are required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service payments to international agencies and sub-consultants, the preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 using priority execution (S.W.I.F.T. payment messages) settled in USD, EUR, or GBP. For media purchase commitments, banks support documentary collections and standby letters of credit, while commercial LCs are available for high-value production contracts. Domestic payroll is run via the NZ Clearing System (Direct Debit / Direct Credit) using the bank's online platform. Outbound wires must carry accurate purpose codes (e.g., 'Royalties', 'Professional Services') to avoid bank rejections. The bank will evaluate FX conversion at market rate with consideration for settlement date.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outward forward contracts (plain vanilla forwards) for up to 12 months to lock in client retainer receipts in foreign currencies
FX swaps to manage NZD/foreign currency liquidity mismatches between retainer invoicing and advertising purchases
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for any senior debt in non-NZD (subject to credit committee approval)

No NDFs for NZD/foreign pairs are market standard because the NZD is freely deliverable; NDFs are only used for emerging market pairs with no local delivery, and NZD cannot be the non-deliverable leg in a compliant structure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Companies Act 1993, s 208 - annual company renewal and confirmation statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZ Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment - MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days after the annual return date, which is the last day of the month of the company's incorporation anniversary; filing is mandatory even when no company details have changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the annual return is not filed by the due date, the Registrar issues a default notice and a late filing fee applies. Continued failure to file for two consecutive annual return periods authorises the Registrar to commence strike-off under Companies Act 1993, s 318, after 20 working days' notice. A struck-off company loses separate legal personality, its property may pass to the Crown as bona vacantia, and directors face disqualification risks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (IR4 and IR10 if required) together with terminal or provisional tax payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the annual income tax return is due by 7 July immediately following the balance date. Provisional tax instalments for standard-balance-date taxpayers fall due at 28 August, 15 January and 7 April during the relevant income year cycle; a tax agent extension may apply in certain prescribed circumstances.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties apply for returns not filed by the due date, currently NZ$50 per return. Late payment triggers an initial penalty of 1% on the first day, an additional 4% at day 7, and a further 1% per month on the unpaid balance. Non-payment can expose directors to personal liability in respect of withholding-type taxes and general IRD enforcement action, including prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements and financial statement filing for companies exceeding the statutory 'large company' threshold, or otherwise required to file audited accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies at the New Zealand Companies Office; shareholder requisition if voluntary audit is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a large company, audited financial statements must be completed and delivered to the Registrar within 6 months after the balance date; for a 31 March balance date, this means no later than 30 September of the same year. Small exempt non-issuer companies are not required to file audited financial statements with the Registrar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file required audited financial statements within the statutory window is an offence under the Companies Act 1993. Directors may be liable for fines of up to NZ$10,000 per director on conviction, and the Registrar may treat persistent non-compliance as an additional ground for deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified New Zealand statutory auditor is mandatory where the entity is an issuer, holds public accountability, or qualifies as a 'large company' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. A company is 'large' when it satisfies at least two of the following criteria in each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods: (a) total assets exceed NZ$60,000,000; (b) total revenue exceeds NZ$30,000,000; (c) 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. A smaller company is still compelled to appoint an auditor if shareholders holding 5% or more of the voting shares give written notice requiring an audit, or if the company's constitution mandates one. The audit must be performed by a licensed auditor under the Auditor Regulation Act 2011 and in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (New Zealand).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial reporting is governed by the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the External Reporting Board's (XRB) Accounting Standards Framework: Tier 1 applies New Zealand IFRS; Tier 2 applies New Zealand equivalents to IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regimes (NZ IFRS RDR); Tier 3 applies simple format reporting on an accrual basis; and Tier 4 applies simple format reporting on a cash basis for the smallest for-profit entities. Large non-issuer companies ordinarily report under NZ IFRS or NZ IFRS RDR; all financial statements must give a true and fair view.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a standalone 30-day UBO portal or separate public beneficial-owner annual return. The Companies Act 1993, s 205, instead requires each annual return to confirm the full current shareholding register, the names and addresses of all directors, and the registered office. Share transfers are effective only when entered in the company's own share register, and the register must be updated without undue delay after settlement; changes to directors, registered office and other prescribed particulars are notifiable to the Companies Office within 20 working days. For AML/CFT-reporting entities, beneficial ownership information must be obtained through customer due diligence at the prescribed points, and the share register and annual return form the statutory record of ownership for corporate law purposes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Directors' and Shareholders' Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 850 per year for registered office and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for a small exempt non-issuer company; USD 6,000 - 25,000 per year if a qualified New Zealand statutory audit becomes mandatory or is validly requisitioned by shareholders.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays for standard PR agencies. Eligible R&D tax credit of 15% on qualifying R&D expenditure may reduce effective tax burden. Limited imputation credit system provides shareholder-level integration; no tax preference for income from public relations services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRD Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed via myIR or approved software gateway
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fourth month after the company's balance date, unless an extension of time has been granted for tax agents (usually by 31 March following the income year for standard 31 March balance dates)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income for the income year derived from all business sources under ordinary concepts, including services fees from overseas clients
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose New Zealand-sourced gross income and all worldwide income derived by the New Zealand resident company; do not exclude foreign-source income unless specifically exempt under the deemed source rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income before expenses and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any assessable income arising from activities conducted through a New Zealand fixed establishment and ensure alignment with the financial statements

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenditure and deductions claimed, including operating costs, rent, salaries, professional services, and depreciation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses that are genuinely incurred by the New Zealand entity for the production of assessable income and that are commercially reasonable; reject head-office cost allocations lacking transfer pricing documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before allowing for tax losses carried forward and loss offsets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that any loss offset with a foreign related party is supported by a valid loss offset election and reflects arm's length conditions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income after deducting available loss offsets, including tax losses carried forward within the five-year limitation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the relevant loss continuity schedule; ensure 49% or more continuity of ultimate shareholding if the PR firm is held by a non-resident parent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable at 28% before imputation credits, foreign tax credits, and provisional tax offsets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute at the statutory rate; no special lower rate applies to non-resident-owned companies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits attached to dividends received from other New Zealand resident companies and available to offset company tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include imputation credits from genuine New Zealand resident companies; verify beneficiary and imputation ratio documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits claimed for income taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions on foreign-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim must be restricted to New Zealand income tax payable on the same foreign-source income; maintain underlying foreign tax assessment documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subpart F income and controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution adjustments, if applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not typical for a PR agency but must be completed if the NZ company holds an interest in a foreign CFC with passive income; use Form CFC disclosure schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax credits and supplementary dividend gross-up calculations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Relevant only for inbound dividends from foreign subsidiaries; reconcile with treaty relief claims

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior income years and the amount used this year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Subject to the five-year loss carryforward limit and the shareholder continuity test; attach the IR4 loss schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax paid instalments and residual income tax reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure provisional tax instalments for the non-resident-owned PR company are made under the standard uplift method or the ratio method according to IRD notice

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax avoidance disclosure flag and related-party transaction disclosures under section GC of the Income Tax Act 2007
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Failures to disclose material cross-border related-party transactions will trigger heightened IRD transfer pricing review

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 exposes the company to an initial late filing penalty of NZD 250, plus an automatic late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid tax per month and an incremental penalty of 4% per six-monthly period on amounts still outstanding after the grace period. Intentional non-filing may lead to shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall, plus interest on unpaid tax at the IRD prescribed rate, and criminal prosecution for evasion where intent is established.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 28% (New Zealand resident withholding tax on dividends is imposed at the company tax rate, but the imputation credit system typically extinguishes the resident withholding tax liability when fully imputed dividends are distributed. For non-resident shareholders, the gross dividend is subject to non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) capped at the applicable treaty rate, usually 15% under the OECD Model treaty pattern, with Australia at 5% for significant shareholdings and 15% otherwise).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident parent company must submit a valid New Zealand IRD Form IR3NRWT or an equivalent declaration before the distribution date to enable reduced NRWT under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA). The payor company must also hold a copy of the parent's tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. If the DTA relief requires a specific procedure, the IRD Commissioner must issue a certificate of reduced NRWT or a notice of satisfaction of conditions before the dividend is paid. Where the beneficial owner is a resident of a treaty jurisdiction, the rate reduction applies only if the parent provides a completed IRD Form IR290 or a similar certificate, and the New Zealand company must file an NRWT return by the 20th of the month following the payment month. For dividends paid through an intermediary holding company without substantive economic substance, the treaty claim may be denied under the principal purpose test or the limitation on benefits clause.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT is 15% of gross royalties, typically reduced to 10% or 0% under DTAs depending on the treaty partner and beneficial ownership conditions. Interest: statutory NRWT is 15% of gross interest, generally reduced to 10% under most DTAs, and commonly 0% under the Australia and Singapore treaties where the interest is not attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment. Approved issuer levy (AIL) at 2% may apply as an alternative to NRWT on interest paid to non-residents by an approved issuer if the interest is not otherwise subject to NRWT or where an eligible exemption applies. All treaty relief claims require the payor to hold the recipient's TRC and to substantiate beneficial ownership, and no anti-treaty-shopping provision may be breached.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 annual group turnover threshold for mandatory Master File and Local File documentation under New Zealand's transfer pricing rules; documentation is also required for all cross-border related-party transactions with an aggregated annual value exceeding NZD 1,000,000 where the IRD deems the arrangement high risk, although the formal documentation threshold is aligned with OECD guidance at the NZD 10 million group revenue level. In all cases, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be prepared before the tax return filing date.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE or Barbados, but the IRD applies general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) under section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and transfer pricing rules under sections GC 13 to GC 15 of the Income Tax Act 2007, which mandate that cross-border related-party arrangements achieve an arm's length result. A New Zealand PR agency with a non-resident parent must demonstrate real operational substance, including active client contracts, locally employed professional staff, genuine decision-making authority for the PR engagement, and a substantive New Zealand profit margin for the functions performed. Companies that function as shell entities or that accept low functional margins without local economic substance face recharacterization, additional tax assessments, and penalty exposure. The OECD's principal purpose test and the Multilateral Instrument (MLI) also apply to deny treaty benefits where the main purpose of an arrangement is tax avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting client income from retainer fees, understating cross-border service revenue, falsifying invoices, or destroying books and records with intent to evade New Zealand income tax and GST
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under section 143 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, with imprisonment of up to 5 years, plus a criminal fine of up to NZD 50,000 and an additional penalty of treble the evaded tax shortfall (150% shortfall penalty on top of the tax itself)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in evasion face personal criminal liability, imprisonment up to 5 years, and civil restitution for the evaded tax, including interest and penalties; travel bans may be sought by the IRD as a debt collection measure under section 34A of the Tax Administration Act 1994

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a New Zealand company that does not perform substantive PR functions, has no real staff or office, merely books intercompany retainer fees, and is used primarily to claim treaty benefits or shift profits while lacking local commercial substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the arrangement under the GAAR or transfer pricing reallocation, resulting in additional taxable income, interest, and shortfall penalties up to 150%; denial of double tax relief and loss of imputation credit management status; possible removal from the New Zealand companies register under the Companies Act 1993 for serious non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the unpaid tax of a shell company if they allowed the company to operate while insolvent or engaged in phoenix-company behavior; they may face civil penalty proceedings under the Companies Act 1993 and disqualification for up to 10 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large retainer payments from overseas politically exposed persons or from jurisdictions on the FATF blacklist without performing customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining written AML/CFT compliance programs under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to NZD 4 million for a company, plus NZD 1 million for each individual involved, per contravention; criminal liability with imprisonment up to 5 years for deliberate money laundering or terrorist financing facilitation under the Crimes Act 1961 and the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability for willful blindness or participation in AML failures, including fines and up to 5 years imprisonment, as well as disqualification from managing companies under the Companies Act 1993

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to document cross-border related-party transactions, charging intercompany management fees or royalty-like retainer-flow arrangements that do not reflect the arm's length principle, or manipulating the New Zealand company's profit level to artificially shift value offshore
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under sections GC 13-15 of the Income Tax Act 2007, with the Commissioner determining an arm's length result, imposing additional tax, paying prescribed interest from the original due date, and a shortfall penalty of up to 150% for gross carelessness or intentional behavior; document deficiencies attract a separate documentation penalty of up to NZD 20,000 per year
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign inaccurate tax returns or knowingly authorize false transfer-pricing documentation become jointly and severally liable for the shortfall penalties and interest if the corporate veil is pierced; serious cases trigger director disqualification and personal non-asset-procedure proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Reporting of Foreign Bank Accounts and International Transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to disclose overseas bank accounts, foreign trusts, or non-resident related-party payments to the IRD in the annual IRD disclosure schedules, or failing to file an IRD form IR3NR and NRWT returns in respect of foreign debt and equity interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late payment penalties of up to 150% of the unpaid withholding tax, late filing penalties, and prescribed interest; where the omission is deliberate, criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994 with imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally admonished through the IRD's director penalty notice procedure, making them personally liable for unpaid PAYE and certain withholding amounts under section 156 of the Tax Administration Act 1994; the notice may be followed by civil asset recovery and travel restriction procedures

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Breach of Statutory Document Destruction Rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying, altering, or concealing invoices, contracts, bank statements, or electronic records that evidence PR retainer fees, cross-border charges, or tax computations, particularly within the seven-year statutory record-keeping period
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to NZD 40,000 under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and an additional shortfall penalty of 150% if the destruction was intended to obstruct the IRD; individual directors face imprisonment of up to 5 years for perverting the course of justice
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director who directs, approves, or knowingly assists in the destruction of tax records is personally liable for fines and imprisonment, and will be subject to civil penalties for the value of the tax shortfall caused, with the corporate veil pierced under the equitable fraud exception
